key_insight: Machine learning can diagnose degradation mechanisms in simulated lead-free RbSn₀.₅Ge₀.₅I₃ solar cells from temperature- and illumination-dependent open-circuit voltage measurements.
engineering_relevance: The approach could support post-fabrication fault diagnosis, while simulations indicate that replacing Spiro-OMeTAD with CuI raises efficiency from 19.6% to 21.6%, mainly through improved fill factor.
method: Compare forward surrogate models trained on factorial grids and Latin hypercube samples.
Use multi-label classification to identify six degradation mechanisms from voltage measurements.
evidence_signal: The diagnostic classifier achieved macro F1 = 0.938 versus 0.687 for physics rules; forward-model R² fell from 0.9997 on held-out grid points to 0.58 on independent samples, while Latin hypercube training restored R² to 0.995.
watch_item: Results are simulation-based, and the diagnostic classifier failed to generalize to degradation-mechanism combinations absent from training.
paper_title: Interpretable machine learning diagnosis of degradation mechanisms in lead-free $RbSn_{0.5}Ge_{0.5}I_{3}$ solar cells from temperature- and illumination-dependent electrical measurements
